observations.text: SP, due to a study method that relied on memorized answers rather than on the source publications, could not locate in the Flight Manual and in the aeronautical publications the route data requested at the pre-flight briefing, with the result that the IP had to direct the SP to the applicable paragraphs and to provide part of the answers. Knowledge of the daily assignment was not demonstrated without assistance. Systematic study from the primary handbooks is required.

SP, due to lack of knowledge of the published procedure for the condition encountered, could not explain the low-level VFR altitude and weather minima of AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 applicable to the planned route, with the result that the IP had to state the limits and the route restrictions during the pre-flight briefing. The same items could not be answered at the post-flight briefing without assistance. Further study of the navigation-related publications is required.

SP demonstrated the general knowledge required for this stage of the Training Section; however, the answers on the chart symbology and on the MAIP data for the alternate airfield were completed only after the IP's verbal prompts, and two references were located with delay. The daily assignment was known in outline but the handbooks were not yet used with confidence. Marginal performance for this stage - independent use of the Flight Manual and of the aeronautical publications is expected to improve.

SP answered the questions on the route publications, on the meteorological briefing data and on the airport traffic procedures with minor errors, which were recognized and corrected by the SP without IP's intervention. The daily assignment was known and the applicable handbook paragraphs were located without prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated detailed and accurate knowledge of the Flight Manual, of the Techniques and Procedures Manual and of the aeronautical publications applicable to the planned route, answering promptly at the pre-flight briefing and during the flight. Meteorological principles, aerodynamics and airport traffic procedures were explained correctly and with confidence, without IP's assistance. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional depth of general knowledge, relating the Flight Manual limits, the AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 provisions and the MAIP data to the specific route and to the forecast conditions of the day. Flight physiology and the sea and land survival and SAR procedures were explained in detail and correlated with the planned low-level profile, at a level above that expected for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to preparation limited to drawing the route without study of the associated publications, could not present the terrain clearance and airspace data required at the pre-flight briefing, with the result that the IP had to direct the study and to provide the applicable MAIP entries. The daily assignment was not covered to a level allowing an independent brief. Further study before the next sortie is required.

SP, due to lack of awareness of a published restriction that was available in the briefing material, could not state the restriction applicable to the second leg when questioned in flight, with the result that the IP had to provide the restriction and to direct the corresponding route adjustment. The same item was not explained at the post-flight briefing without assistance. Detailed study of the aeronautical publications for every route is required.

SP, due to briefing preparation that did not cover the meteorological products for the route, described the forecast conditions only in general terms and did not relate them to the planned leg altitudes, with the result that the complete answer was given only after the IP's verbal prompts. The visibility and turbulence limits applicable to the low-level segment were identified with delay. Study of the morning meteorological briefing material is required.

SP, due to complacency on a route flown repeatedly without incident, did not review the current MAIP data before the sortie and quoted a superseded frequency and an outdated restriction, with the result that the correct data were established only after the IP's verbal prompts. The error was recognized and corrected with delay at the post-flight briefing. Verification of current publications before each sortie is required.

SP demonstrated the general knowledge required for this stage of the Training Section; however, the explanation of the aerodynamic effects of the low-level profile and of the fuel planning method contained minor errors, which were recognized and corrected by the SP without IP's intervention. Use of the Techniques and Procedures Manual was correct but not yet fluent. Marginal performance for this stage - greater confidence in the flight-related handbooks is expected to improve.

SP knew in detail the daily assignment and answered accurately and promptly on the Flight Manual limits, on the AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 provisions and on the aeronautical publications applicable to the route, at the pre-flight briefing, in flight and at the post-flight briefing. The meteorological and aerodynamic questions were explained correctly without IP's assistance. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional general knowledge, using the Flight Manual, the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the MAIP with confidence and correlating them with the specific route, the forecast weather and the fuel plan. Flight physiology and the sea and land survival and SAR procedures were explained in detail and applied to the planned navigation area, above the level expected for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to study that did not extend beyond the material of the previous training section, could not answer the questions on the emergency airfields, on the SAR coverage and on the survival equipment applicable to the navigation route, with the result that the IP had to provide the data and to conduct the corresponding part of the pre-flight briefing. The handbooks required by BD 3-1/HATC were not used with confidence. A structured review of the navigation-related publications is required.

SP, due to lack of knowledge of the published procedure for the condition encountered, could not state the lost procedure and the diversion actions required by the applicable publications when questioned during the flight, with the result that the IP had to direct the procedure and to execute part of the diversion planning. The corresponding paragraphs could not be located at the post-flight briefing without assistance. Further study of the applicable handbooks is required.

SP, due to reliance on personal notes instead of the source publications, presented the airport traffic procedures and the flight planning data for the destination incompletely, with the result that the briefing was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts and the correct references were located with delay. Knowledge of the daily assignment was demonstrated only in part. Study directly from the Flight Manual and the MAIP is required.

SP, due to reliance on the automated navigation solution in place of knowledge of the published route data, could not explain the minimum safe altitudes and the airspace boundaries of the legs from the chart when questioned in flight, with the result that the data were established only after the IP's verbal prompts. The difference between the loaded route and the published restrictions was recognized with delay. Chart-based route knowledge independent of the equipment is required.

SP, due to briefing preparation that treated the meteorological products separately from the route profile, explained the forecast wind and visibility without relating them to the leg altitudes and timing, with the result of a minor error in the expected drift, which was recognized and corrected by the SP without IP's intervention. The remaining questions on the publications and on the Flight Manual limits were answered accurately.

SP, due to reliance on how the route is habitually flown rather than on the published criteria, quoted the entry procedure for the low-level segment from local practice and not from the applicable publication, with the result of a minor error in the stated entry altitude, which was recognized and corrected by the SP without IP's intervention. The remaining answers on the Techniques and Procedures Manual and on AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 were accurate and prompt.

SP demonstrated accurate and prompt general knowledge within the standards of the Training Section; however, the answers on flight physiology and on the sea survival procedures were given after noticeable hesitation and one reference was located with delay. All items were finally answered correctly and without IP's assistance. Marginal performance for this stage - the fluency shown on the route and Flight Manual questions is expected to extend to the survival and physiology material.

SP demonstrated exceptional general knowledge across the Flight Manual, the Techniques and Procedures Manual, AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 and the aeronautical publications, using them with confidence at the pre-flight briefing, in flight and at the post-flight briefing. Meteorological principles, aerodynamics, flight physiology and the sea and land survival and SAR procedures were explained in detail and correlated with the specific navigation route and with the conditions of the day. Above end of block MIF achieved.
